title: RE Sang Bai Kim and RE Chan Soo Kim v. Korean Eastern Presbytery
disposition_detail: Issue 1: KEP's denial of the appeal and sustaining of the CPC judgment—affirmed; specified BCO errors not sustained. Issue 2: KEP's increase of censures from suspension from sacraments and office to deposition and excommunication—reversed; the appellate court lacked authority under BCO 42-9 to increase, and the trial court retained discretion to remove or increase an indefinite suspension. No remand is stated in the judgment.
first_summary: Two ruling elders disciplined after a Korean Eastern Presbytery election dispute appealed to the SJC. The SJC affirmed KEP's denial of their appeal and the session's guilt findings, but reversed KEP's increase of the censures to deposition and excommunication. It held that an appellate court cannot increase a censure. The original suspension from communion and office remained.
summary: In a dispute arising from a Korean Eastern Presbytery congregational election, two ruling elders were tried, refused to plead, and were suspended from sacraments and office; KEP denied their appeal, then increased the censures to deposition and excommunication for contumacy. The SJC affirmed KEP's denial and the guilt findings, but reversed the increased censures. An appellate court may not increase a censure under BCO 42-9; the trial court retains discretion to remove or increase an indefinite suspension, though the appellate court may recommend a lesser censure. The original suspension remained.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 2002-01, RE Sang Bai Kim and RE Chan Soo Kim v. Korean Eastern Presbytery, decided by the SJC for the 31st GA (2003); the panel prepared the summary, issues, and judgment, and the full SJC extensively amended the statement and reasoning. Lines 1–3, 14, 112–118; source cases/ga31_2003__2002-01.md, sha256 88dc69ff104a91a6d3bc11980a4b765abd3686e870eaf72ed71223c88a12a75a.
evidence_notes.dispute: The same parties as SJC 2001-06; after a contested CPC congregational election, the two elders not elected held emergency session meetings, suspended members, and were charged; after refusing to plead at trial they were found guilty and suspended from communion. KEP denied their appeal, then increased censures to deposition and excommunication. Lines 20–52, 56–58.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Judgment: issue 1—No, KEP did not err in denying the appeal/sustaining CPC; specified BCO errors not sustained, KEP affirmed in whole. Issue 2—Yes, KEP erred by increasing censures. The SJC reasoned that an appellate court cannot increase a censure, BCO 42-9 gives no such power, and only the trial court may remove or increase an indefinite suspension; an appellate court may recommend a lesser censure. Lines 60–64, 86–110.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The panel noted Korean-language and cultural complications, accepted the clerk's certified translations, and disregarded claims of fraudulent, inaccurate, or biased translation. The reasoning was written by TE Lunceford with concurrence and extensively amended by the full SJC. The header notes a dissent, but no separate dissent text appears in the supplied excerpt. Lines 68–82, 112–118, line 3.

Central Carolina Presbytery) is cited for the proposition that an appellate court may recommend a lesser censure; that decision is not supplied. Lines 20, 107–110.
